clue.text: Liaison gets a fellow just ecstatic at the outset

parts.note: just in the sense of fair-minded, equitable

indicators.note: at the outset points to the opening letter of the word ecstatic

explanation.surface: Someone's love affair finds a man thrilled from the very start.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word is used in English for a romantic or sexual affair, a liaison.

clue.text: Sneaking low punch over top of groin

parts.note: to low is to make a cow's sound, moo
to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of the word groin is its first letter

explanation.surface: A boxer throws a sneaky low blow aimed at the groin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' simply places the pieces one above the other in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To mooch is to slink or loiter furtively, so mooching is skulking about.

clue.text: Zoroastrian changing direction finally breaks down

indicators.note: changing tells us a letter of the Zoroastrian is swapped for the direction, and finally places it at the end

parts.note: a Parsee is an Indian follower of Zoroaster
S for south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A Zoroastrian who swaps his course ends up collapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' says it is the last letter, E, that 'changing' replaces with S.
explanation.definitionFit: To parse a sentence is to analyse it grammatically, breaking it into its component parts.

clue.text: Feed up, then start to lose weight

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for feed is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to feed is to eat

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word lose

explanation.surface: Advice to a dieter: eat up, then begin shedding pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A tael is an East Asian unit of weight, used especially for silver.

clue.text: Sound of snake slipped under queen

indicators.note: in a down clue, slipped under puts the snake below the queen's letter

parts.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: A snake slithers beneath a queen, recalling Cleopatra's end.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a harsh grating noise.

clue.text: Salty act upset agent

indicators.note: upset signals that the letters of salty act are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A salty performance has upset a theatrical agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A catalyst is a substance or person that brings about change, an agent of reaction.

clue.text: Coleridge Rime ultimately about a sea bird means the poet's everlasting

indicators.note: about means the two final letters go around the sea bird
ultimately points to the final letter of each of the words Coleridge and Rime

parts.note: a tern is a sea bird

explanation.surface: Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner, with its albatross, is a timeless poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites the albatross, but the bird here is a TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic form of eternal survives in verse, so it is a poetic word for everlasting.

clue.text: More than one bust attracts attention

explanation.definitionFit: Busts are police arrests, plural; and something that arrests the eye catches it, attracting attention.

clue.text: Goodness me, football's ruling body's engaged Robson!

indicators.note: engaged in the sense of occupied, so the football body holds the exclamation inside it

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which runs English football
lor is an old exclamation of surprise, short for Lord

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that the FA has hired the footballer Robson.
explanation.walkthrough: Robson suggests football's Bryan or Bobby Robson; the definition is the actress Dame Flora Robson.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Flora Robson was a celebrated English stage and film actress; Robson is her surname.

clue.text: A laboratory plant is translucent white

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flowering plant

explanation.surface: A plant grown in a lab is pale and see-through.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine-grained mineral prized for its pale, glowing, semi-transparent appearance.

clue.text: Charge account about covers American loan's first instalment

indicators.note: covers means the abbreviation for about is wrapped round the American

parts.note: CA for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: first instalment of a word is its opening letter, here of loan

explanation.surface: A bank statement shows charges about covering the first instalment of an American loan.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusal is an accusation, a charge laid against someone.

clue.text: Power that is inflated, that's plain

annotationWithheld.why: Power that is inflated, that's plain (7): the wordplay needs PR + AIR + IE, and no standard reading turns 'Power' into PR; a word such as 'right' may be missing from the clue as held.
annotationWithheld.clue: Power that is inflated, that's plain

clue.text: Sure distressed about eimi's having discounted me for further publication

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around what is left of the Greek word
distressed signals that the letters of the word sure are thrown into disorder
having discounted means the note is taken out of the letters of eimi's

parts.note: eimi is Greek for I am; the possessive s is kept as a letter here
me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone is upset about a Greek verb for a reprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' and 'mi' are alternative spellings of the same sol-fa note, so the note removed is spelt MI; the surface's Greek 'I am' hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a new release of a book or record, a further publication.

clue.text: Guard denied second admission …

indicators.note: denied means the guard is refused the letter for second

parts.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard

explanation.surface: A guard turned away for a moment refuses someone entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry and admission both mean being let in.

clue.text: Perhaps rent books come with demand for money

parts.note: Pay me! is what someone demanding money says
NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A landlord hands over the rent book while asking for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks rent as one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is one kind of sum handed over regularly, an example of money paid.

clue.text: … concealed in doorkeeper duty

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies inside the run of letters doorkeeper duty

explanation.surface: Something is concealed while the doorkeeper is on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Perdu, from French, means hidden away or lying in ambush.

clue.text: Possibly worthiest to penetrate the heart of autobiographical author

indicators.note: to penetrate means the rearranged letters push inside the central letters
the heart of a long word is its central letters, here the middle pair of autobiographical
possibly signals that the letters of worthiest may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: The most deserving writer gets to the core of an autobiography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'autobiographical' looks like part of the definition, but its heart, the middle pair of letters, is the container; 'Possibly' rearranges the nine letters that slot inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostwriter is the hidden writer of a book credited to someone else, often an autobiography.

clue.text: Oddly discarded poor tiger, not, sadly, a long-tailed cat

indicators.note: oddly discarded means the odd-numbered letters of poor tiger not sadly are thrown away, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A sad tale of a poor tiger that is no longer around.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oriental is a slender cat breed with a notably long, whip-like tail.

clue.text: Row over a driver first of all changing gear?

definitions.text: Row over a driver first of all changing gear?

indicators.note: first of all points to the opening letters of row over a driver
changing signals that the letters of gear are rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist's argument sparked by a gear change.
explanation.definitionFit: Road rage is the angry, aggressive behaviour of motorists, such as rows between drivers.

clue.text: Hopefully 'I'm pickin' up good vibrations'

parts.note: the Beach Boys lyric seems to be about mood, but read literally it is a body part saying it detects sound waves

explanation.definitionFit: The tympanic membrane vibrates when sound waves strike it, passing the sound on to the inner ear.

clue.text: Is inclined to enter church to get rid of guilt

indicators.note: to enter means the leaning word goes inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
leans means is inclined or tilted

explanation.surface: A guilty person is minded to go to church for absolution.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to purify, as of sin or guilt.

clue.text: Bitterness of detective inspector in Oxford, for example

indicators.note: in places the detective inspector inside the city

parts.note: Oxford is a city, so a city

explanation.surface: Resentment felt by a police inspector working in Oxford, as in Inspector Morse.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse was a fictional Oxford detective (a chief inspector) on British TV, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidity is sourness or sharpness, of taste or temper.

clue.text: In my cases there's absolutely nothing at all to indicate shocking misconduct

indicators.note: cases means the words in my enclose the slang for nothing

parts.note: FA, from sweet FA, is British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: A suspect insists nothing in their case points to wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet FA' is a British euphemism meaning nothing whatsoever.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is notoriety, or an act of outrageous wickedness.

clue.text: To rectify a confused state requires peacekeepers to show teeth

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
to snarl is to bare the teeth

explanation.surface: Sorting out a muddle needs peacekeepers willing to bare their teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsnarl is to untangle, putting a muddle straight.

clue.text: Wrap scraps of cloth up round silver box for protection

indicators.note: round means the reversed rags go around the symbol for silver
in a down clue up means the rags are read from bottom to top

parts.note: rags are scraps of cloth
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Instructions for wrapping silverware in rags and storing it in a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap' merely opens the instruction; 'up' reads the rags from bottom to top, giving SGAR, before they go round the silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A saggar is a fireclay case that shields pottery while it is fired in a kiln.

clue.text: Splendid senorita's outlines

parts.note: def is slang for excellent or splendid
Ines is a Spanish girl's name, so stands for a senorita

explanation.surface: A Spanish girl's splendid figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A senorita is a young Spanish woman; INES stands for one by example, without a 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Defines and outlines both mean marks out the limits or describes the shape.

clue.text: Venture to mix in prison

explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to venture out of doors; to stir is also to mix; and stir is old slang for prison.

clue.text: Solicit occasional Celtic euphemistic exclamation

parts.note: to solicit is to beg
orra is a Scots word meaning odd or occasional

explanation.surface: A request for an occasional Celtic oath.
explanation.walkthrough: ORRA is a Scots word, which fits the Celtic surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This Irish oath is a minced form of By God, a euphemism for swearing.

clue.text: Old chariot's not enough for Abigail

indicators.note: not enough for means only part of the name Abigail is used, letters from within it

explanation.surface: A vintage chariot is too small for Abigail.
explanation.definitionFit: A biga was a Roman two-horse chariot.

clue.text: Expressionless gunmen in a convertible

indicators.note: convertible means the letters of gunmen in a can be changed into another word

explanation.surface: Blank-faced gunmen sit in a convertible car.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmeaning means vacant or without meaning, as in a blank, expressionless face.

clue.text: Area on North Sea primarily containing good university

definitions.text: Area on North Sea primarily containing good university

indicators.note: containing means those initials hold the abbreviations inside
primarily points to the first letters of area, north and sea

explanation.surface: A coastal region on the North Sea that is home to a fine university.
explanation.walkthrough: ANGUS is a council area on Scotland's east coast, north of Dundee.
explanation.definitionFit: Angus is a Scottish region whose coastline faces the North Sea.
